_doc: Stream E (M2). Wayside dressing: tiny sites with no encounter — a cairn, a milestone, a ribboned tree — that the placer drops into the emptiest stretches so no walk goes more than 250 m without something to notice (PLAN §16 'longest boring walk'). Placement type `wayside` with `id` = one of these ids + a suffix and `kind` = the id here. Props are drawn exactly like a vignette's (same kit ids, offsets rotated by yaw with vignettePoint). `lore` is shown when you walk within `radius` (optional). `biomes` = where it fits best (any if none fit).

kinds.name: Cairn
kinds.lore: Somebody stacked these stones. Everyone who passes adds one. You add one.

kinds.name: Milestone
kinds.lore: A worn stone with a number on it. The number has been argued about for a hundred years.

kinds.name: Ribbon Tree
kinds.lore: Every branch has a ribbon tied to it. Wishes, mostly. One just says 'more cheese'.

kinds.name: Cold Campfire
kinds.lore: A ring of stones, old ash, and a spoon nobody came back for.

kinds.name: Broken Wheel
kinds.lore: A cart wheel, split in two. The rest of the cart got where it was going. Probably.

kinds.name: Old Bones
kinds.lore: Something big died here a long time ago. Something bigger ate it.

kinds.name: Standing Stone
kinds.lore: One tall stone, leaning. It has been leaning for so long it may be doing it on purpose.

kinds.name: Mushroom Ring
kinds.lore: A perfect ring of mushrooms. The old stories say don't step inside. The old stories are very bossy.

kinds.name: Fallen Pillar
kinds.lore: A carved pillar lying in the grass, miles from anything it could have held up.

kinds.name: Lost Signpost
kinds.lore: A signpost with every arm snapped off. It points nowhere, firmly.

kinds.name: Hunter's Rack
kinds.lore: An empty drying rack and a stump to sit on. The hunter will be back. Or won't.

kinds.name: Dolmen
kinds.lore: Three stones and a lid. Old as the hills, and the hills are not saying.

kinds.name: Boundary Stakes
kinds.lore: A line of stakes marking somebody's land. Somebody very sure of themselves.

kinds.name: Wind Shrine
kinds.lore: A little arch of stones the wind sings through. Leave a pebble; take a tune.

kinds.name: Shrine Niche
kinds.lore: A hollow in a roadside stone with a stub of candle in it. Somebody lit it this week.

kinds.name: Old Toll Stone
kinds.lore: A stone carved with prices for a toll nobody has collected in years. Sheep: a penny. Geese: two. Bishops: ask.

kinds.name: Scarecrow
kinds.lore: A scarecrow in a good coat. Better than yours. The crows sit on it anyway.

kinds.name: Roadside Grave
kinds.lore: A low mound with a plank at its head. The name has weathered off. The flowers are fresh.

kinds.name: League Stone
kinds.lore: A tall marker cut with an arrow and a number. The number has been chipped and re-cut so many times it is mostly hole.

kinds.name: Fallen Tree
kinds.lore: A great trunk across the verge with two axes still in it. The woodcutters stopped for lunch and have not come back.

kinds.name: Sheep Pen
kinds.lore: A hurdle pen with the gate tied shut with string. Inside: one sheep, looking at you like this is your fault.

kinds.name: Beehive Row
kinds.lore: Three straw skeps on a plank, humming. A sign says HONEY FOR SALE and then, smaller, ASK THE BEES.

kinds.name: Hay Rick
kinds.lore: A rick of hay roped against the weather. Something has burrowed into the side and made itself comfortable.

kinds.name: Ruined Cottage
kinds.lore: Two walls of a cottage meeting in a corner, a doorstep with no door. Nettles have moved in.

kinds.name: Bridge Pier
kinds.lore: A stone pier for a bridge that was never built, or was built and left. Either way it is very sure of itself.

kinds.name: Wayside Well
kinds.lore: A well by the road with a tin cup chained to it. The chain is newer than the cup.

kinds.name: Abandoned Cart
kinds.lore: A cart with no horse and no wheels, slowly turning into a shed for weeds.

kinds.name: Faded Banner
kinds.lore: A pole with a banner bleached to no colour at all. Whoever it stood for is no longer anyone.

kinds.name: Stone Trough
kinds.lore: A long stone trough full of rainwater and one optimistic frog.

kinds.name: Woodpile
kinds.lore: A neat stack of split logs under a bark roof, and a carved sign: TAKE ONE, LEAVE ONE. Somebody took six.

kinds.name: Snow Pole
kinds.lore: A tall striped pole so travellers can find the road under the snow. It leans the way the wind usually goes.

kinds.name: Driftwood Post
kinds.lore: A post of bleached driftwood hung with shells, net floats and one shoe.
